methodsMarkdown:
## Pooled analyses of two trials

These findings combine the two Chicago randomized tutoring studies reported in the final AER article. They are additional analyses of those trials, not a third experiment. ITT estimates the effect of a tutoring offer; TOT uses randomized assignment as an instrument for participation. Alternate estimands and pooled results must not be counted as independent evidence.

## Follow-up and uncertainty

Table 5 reports the first postrandomization school year. Table 7 measures eleventh-grade outcomes in the year students would have reached that grade without retention, rather than one common elapsed follow-up interval. The authors describe persistent math effects but imprecise graduation effects. The terminal date for the outcome labeled Graduated ever is not yet established; it must not be interpreted as lifetime graduation. Table 7 retains duplicate randomization observations and clusters standard errors by individual.

## Shared statistics and units

The control mean and estimated control-complier mean are different quantities. Reported FDR q-values belong to the source row and must not be relabeled as ordinary per-estimand p-values. Fraction-valued outcomes retain their original scale. The suspension label does not resolve whether its unit is days or events; leave its unit absent rather than inventing one.

## Coverage

[Final AER article](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20210434), Tables 5 and 7, printed pages 751 and 753. Table 6's weighted per-year effect and upper bounds require separate modeling and are not included in these point-estimate tables. Study-specific later outcomes in the appendix remain separate required coverage.
